subject.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access

question: How should OpenClaw handle pre-existing trigger-script jobs that lack toolsAllow because their creator's historical tool policy was never persisted?
rationale: A trustworthy cap cannot be reconstructed from legacy rows; preserving them retains the existing broad tool surface, while fail-closed handling can stop operator automation and requires a recovery design.

options.title: Add legacy-job audit
options.body: Land the forward fix with an operator-visible doctor or startup audit that identifies cap-less triggers and offers explicit remediation.

options.title: Accept forward-only coverage
options.body: Merge while explicitly accepting that historical uncapped triggers remain unrestricted until an authorized agent-tool edit restamps them.

options.title: Fail closed
options.body: Block cap-less legacy trigger evaluation until an operator assigns policy, accepting immediate compatibility impact.

recommendation.title: Add legacy-job audit
recommendation.body: Land the forward fix with an operator-visible doctor or startup audit that identifies cap-less triggers and offers explicit remediation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest available history across the affected cron and trigger-runtime surfaces and is the best individual routing candidate for the security-versus-upgrade choice.
